args: In gpac/src/isomedia/box_code_base.c, what is the safest ownership-preserving way to clear or replace GF_MPEGAudioSampleEntryBox::esd in audio_sample_entry_box_read after gf_isom_box_array_read fails, given that esd may either be directly owned by ptr->child_boxes or alias an ESDS owned by a QuickTime wave child's child_boxes? Are there existing helper APIs to locate/detach a descendant box, or should the fallback only delete esd when it is found directly in ptr->child_boxes?

The sanitizer report shows audio_sample_entry_box_read at line 4053 calling gf_isom_box_del_parent(&ptr->child_boxes, ptr->esd). gf_isom_box_del_parent unconditionally deletes the box even if gf_list_del_item did not find it. audio_sample_entry_on_child_box sets ptr->esd to an ESDS nested under a QuickTime wave box without transferring ownership unless conversion mode is active. Thus line 4053 frees a nested ESDS while wave->child_boxes retains it. I am considering guarding deletion by direct membership and otherwise merely clearing the non-owning alias, then parsing and directly owning the recovered replacement. I want to ensure this matches project ownership/callback conventions and find any relevant existing recursive detach helper.
